cases.title: With natural order switched on, a pit typed P1A is listed straight after P1 and before P2, and SPS2 is listed before SPS10
cases.plan_item: UX-SCHED-06 Pit Schedule natural order, the P1A / SPS refinement (daily card D21 assertion 4; switch linking.pitScheduleNaturalOrder ON, OFF in Tim's file)
cases.expected: With the switch on, three pits placed with PIT and their numbers typed in New Pit (SPS10 at 152000,-80000, P1A at 154000,-80000, SPS2 at 156000,-80000; cover 19.000; three Esc each) print 'Pit placed successfully.' three times. The Pit Schedule then lists P1, P1A, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P9, P10, then C1, SPS2, SPS10 in that order; P1A is never below P2 and SPS10 is never above SPS2.
cases.why_not_unit: The order shown depends on the live schedule window reading the real pits, with the real Settings switch, after live placements with typed numbers.
not_automated: Tim's own file has this switch OFF; this proves the switch-ON setting only. The twin N34_BROKEN (switch off) shows the order Max gets today.
SPS10 is placed first on purpose, so a list in placing order or a plain text sort would put SPS10 above SPS2 and fail.

cases.plan_item: UX-LBL-01 hand-placed label stays, the pit-move half (daily card D13 profile B step 3, switch ON; read as 'no CE tidy moves it', see the header)
cases.expected: With both switches on: the new pipe's start invert text IL 18.000 at P8 is moved by hand 5 mm down; the SPOT LEVEL block 10EC5D is moved onto it as in R16; pit P8 is then moved 10 mm north with MOVE: the pit moves 10 mm and the hand-placed text moves more than 1 mm and no more than 20 mm (carried with its pipe end, never shoved 275 mm clear); CDTIDYLABELS All is then only a PREVIEW closed with Esc (nothing is applied): it counts 'Placed by hand (left alone) 1', lists no 'start invert text would move' line, and the text does not move (0 mm, within 0.5); the drawing holds the same number of objects before and after the preview.
cases.why_not_unit: The hand-placed mark is written by a real AutoCAD MOVE of the text, read by the clash tidy that a real MOVE of the pit sets off, and read again by a live Tidy labels preview in the real drawing (cancelled with Esc, so nothing is applied).
not_automated: The card's literal 'move P8 500 mm and the label is exactly where it was' is not checked: the source carries every pipe text with its pipe end, so it would fail by design (a card wording question for Tim, finding in the batch 4 spec).
The card names 'the pipe label'; this case moves the start invert text because it is the text with a proven clash (R16, N27). The rule marks any pipe text moved on its own.

Tim's own file has both switches OFF; this proves the switch-ON setting only. The twin N31_BROKEN is a contrast with tidy ON and hand-placed protection OFF, not D13's literal profile A (which changes neither switch).
The later CDTIDYLABELS operation is a preview followed by Esc; it does not exercise an applied tidy.
